povs.description: Run the real `pr` binary with a multi-tab -S separator (the exact repro from the fix commit: echo a > a; pr -S$'\t\t\t' a -m a). -m merges the two input files into parallel columns, so init_parameters() enters the columns>1 branch, sees a separator starting with '\t', repoints col_sep_string at the 1-byte column_separator while leaving col_sep_length=3, and print_sep_string() reads 2 bytes past the 1-byte global -- ASan global-buffer-overflow.
povs.exploit_path: -S$'\t\t\t' (separator_string: col_sep_length=3, col_sep_string=optarg_S) -> init_parameters columns>1 branch (col_sep_string = column_separator, col_sep_length NOT reset, src/pr.c:1237) -> print_sep_string (s=col_sep_string, l=col_sep_length=3, reads 2 bytes past the 1-byte global, src/pr.c:2224-2241)

povs.description: Same desynchronization with a separator that *starts with* a tab but contains non-tab chars (-S$'\tXX', length 3): init_parameters() only inspects the first byte ('\t'), so col_sep_string is repointed at the 1-byte column_separator while col_sep_length stays 3, and print_sep_string() reads 2 bytes past the global. Guards against a partial fix that special-cases only all-tab separators instead of the length==1 check the official fix uses.
povs.exploit_path: -S$'\tXX' (col_sep_length=3) -> init_parameters (first byte '\t' -> col_sep_string = column_separator, col_sep_length unchanged=3) -> print_sep_string (reads 3 bytes from the 1-byte global, src/pr.c:2225,2241)
